advisories.title: The refuse-before-Ed25519 ordering that Codex PTCB-V44-S1 required is stated in the repair note but not in the normative derivation or in the roster vector
advisories.observation: Codex's frozen requiredRepair read: 'Add a distinct required vector whose P contains zero occurrences of the exact Linux-version prefix and require refusal before Ed25519 acceptance.' v45 delivers the vector as 'zero linux_banner refuse' and states the ordering in /honestyRepairsFromV44/[0] ('must refuse before Ed25519 acceptance'). The ordering appears nowhere in the normative derivation: /loaderTraces is not on the v45 closed roster and is byte-identical to v44, and kexecAbsenceDerivation carries no order, steps or evaluationOrder field.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: The security property Codex was protecting is fail-closed behaviour on a zero-banner P, and that property is fully captured by the roster vector as named. Ordering is not observable from the derivation's accept/refuse output, and refusal is guaranteed regardless of evaluation order because kconfigSerialization.utsRelease makes kernelRelease equality against kernelReleaseParse of P mandatory, so a zero-banner P cannot satisfy it even if Ed25519 verify runs first. Requiring a specific internal evaluation order would be over-specification in a design contract. Recorded so a future round can decide whether the ordering sentence belongs in the derivation text rather than in a repair note.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional. If the ordering is intended to bind, move it into kexecAbsenceDerivation as an explicit precedence statement; if it is not intended to bind, consider softening the word 'must' in /honestyRepairsFromV44/[0].

advisories.title: g22.testMatrix quantifies over NT-TCB-1..4 while negativeTests carries five entries including NT-TCB-KEXEC
advisories.observation: testMatrix reads 'every complete platformProfile x every taxonomy class x NT-TCB-1..4, or explicit absent/inapplicable proof.' /negativeTests has ids NT-TCB-1, NT-TCB-2, NT-TCB-3, NT-TCB-4 and NT-TCB-KEXEC. NT-TCB-KEXEC therefore sits outside the harness cross-product. Codex noted the same asymmetry in passing in its frozen v43 evidence without raising it as a finding.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: Not introduced by v45; testMatrix is unchanged from v44 and has carried this wording for many generations. NT-TCB-KEXEC is Linux-pathless-specific rather than a per-taxonomy-class cell, so excluding it from a profile x class cross-product is defensible design rather than a coverage hole. Its substance is covered in depth by the 72 named vectors in ikconfigParserVectors: builderAttestation failure, official-header/PE-join failure, signed kexecCapability mismatch and kexec_loaded=1 all have named vectors. One condition in the NT-TCB-KEXEC passProperty, presence of /proc/sys/kernel/kexec_load_disabled, has no named roster vector, but it was never named in any v37-v44 roster either, so it is not a vectorRosterRule violation.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional. A future generation could either state NT-TCB-1..4 plus NT-TCB-KEXEC-where-applicable, or record explicitly why NT-TCB-KEXEC is outside the cross-product.

The repair records are also unambiguous in substance because they name the originating reviewers in parentheses, and I verified against the frozen Codex v44 file that its PTCB-V44-S1 is genuinely the same zero-linux_banner finding as mine, so the joint attribution in [0] is accurate rather than a conflation of two different findings. Cosmetic id-hygiene only.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional. Future repair records could follow the CLAUDE-Vxx-Sy / PTCB-Vxx-Sy form used at v27, v39 and v40.
